chunks: ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn ʿAlī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ṣalt, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād, from al-Ḥalabī, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:

He was asked about a man washing his wife. He said: “Yes, from behind the garment; he should not look at her hair nor at anything of her. And a woman may wash her husband, because when he dies she remains in a waiting period from him, but when she dies, his waiting period from her has ended.”
And about a woman who dies during travel, while no mahram and no women are with her, he said: “She is to be buried as she is, in her clothes.”
And about a man who dies during travel, while no mahram and no men are with him, he said: “He is to be buried as he is, in his clothes.”

key_terms.ذُو مَحْرَمٍ: a person within the prohibited degrees of marriage
key_terms.شَعْرِهَا: her hair, specifically mentioned as not to be looked at
key_terms.عِدَّةٍ: the waiting period connected to marital status after death
key_terms.مِنْ وَرَاءِ الثَّوْبِ: from behind a garment, without direct exposure

ai.seo_question: Can a husband or wife wash their spouse after death, and what is done if someone dies during travel without a mahram or same-gender attendants?
ai.summary: This hadith gives legal rulings concerning the washing and burial of the deceased, especially between spouses and in cases of travel when no appropriate person is present to perform the washing. It distinguishes between the husband and wife in relation to the waiting period and instructs that, where washing cannot properly be done, the deceased is buried in their clothes.
